scenario: AITA: My friend sent me a screenshot of her grades, and I'm upset | The other day my friend texted me: "\[cramberrycat\], look, isn't it beautiful?" and sent me a screenshot of her grades: a column of straight A's. It was only this narrow strip, which means she must've taken the pains to crop the screenshot so only the grade letters showed up: no class names, percentages, or extra stuff. ​ I forgot exactly what I did. I know I was kind of surprised and irritated that she did this. (Who sends their friends screenshots of their grades? Is this a thing? If so, please fill me in.) Granted, we are on the nerdier side of friends and of course we talk about grades, but I felt like this was too much. I might've ignored her text for a few hours because I was afraid I might say something wrong, which would probably mark me as the A-hole, but I can't remember if I did. ​ Some time after she had already sent the screenshot, she texted me "Sorry" so I'm not sure, maybe she realized how I might feel and apologized for crossing some sort of line? (If there is, in fact, such a line?) I eventually replied, "Truly a sight to behold", which was deliberate in that it did not reflect my true feelings at all. ​ But in terms of my feelings, and my non-verbal reaction, AITA? Was I wrong to be so upset by it? I just felt it was kind of annoying and unnecessary. I'm not sure if she did it with the intention of hurting me or making me jealous; I'm less open about my grades than she is, because she gets consistent high A's on tests while I get B+'s to low A's, although formerly I was a high A's student. I just feel like I'm being too sensitive or overanalyzing it, which has been the case many a time in the past.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was wrong to be upset when my friend sent me a screenshot of her grades. She sent me a cropped screenshot showing only straight A's, and I felt surprised and irritated. I ignored her texts for a few hours and eventually replied with "Truly a sight to behold," which wasn't how I really felt. Now I'm wondering if I was being too sensitive or overreacting. First, I need to understand why I felt upset. Maybe it's because she shared something personal, like her grades, in a way that seemed boastful. I'm not sure if she intended to make me jealous or just wanted to share her achievements. I know we talk about grades sometimes, but this felt more intense because she went out of her way to crop the screenshot to only show the grades. I also have to consider my own feelings about my grades. I used to be a high A's student, but now I get B+'s to low A's. Maybe seeing her straight A's made me feel insecure about my own academic performance. That could explain why I was upset. On the other hand, maybe I'm overreacting. Grades are a part of life, and sharing them isn't inherently wrong. But the way she presented it, by cropping the screenshot, might have come off as showing off. I wonder if she realized that this could make others feel uncomfortable or insecure. I also need to think about how I responded. I ignored her texts for a few hours and then gave a non-committal reply. That might have made her feel bad, especially since she later apologized. Maybe I should have communicated my feelings more openly instead of letting it fester. Another angle is to consider the context of our friendship. We're on the nerdier side, so talking about grades is somewhat normal. But there's a line between sharing achievements and flaunting them. I'm not sure where exactly that line is, but her action might have crossed it for me. I also need to reflect on whether my reaction was justified. Was I being too sensitive? Or was it reasonable to feel upset given the circumstances? It's possible that I was projecting my own insecurities onto her actions, making me more upset than necessary. In the end, I think it's important to communicate openly with my friend about how her actions made me feel. That way, we can understand each other's perspectives and avoid similar situations in the future. It's also a good opportunity for me to work on my own self-esteem and not let others' achievements affect me negatively.
